user.title: Household Assistant
user.description: Assist will be able to ask the Household Assistant app. In the app, an admin turns on App settings → Answer Assist; then choose Household Assistant as the conversation agent of a voice assistant (Settings → Voice assistants).

abort.already_configured: The Household Assistant is already set up.

init.title: Household Assistant

data_description.voice_user: A voice satellite doesn't say who is speaking. Its questions are asked as this person, with their access in each app, or not at all. Choose a dedicated user with few rights rather than an admin.
data_description.voice_person_only: Questions from voice satellites use only the tools about that person (their own tasks, food log, …), never household-wide ones (spending, everyone's balances). Questions asked as yourself (the app, the Assist dialog) aren't limited.
data_description.signing_key: The same key as App settings → App-messages signing key in the household apps. Empty: messages aren't signed (any app on Home Assistant's network could answer as the assistant).
data_description.timeout: A model on the Home Assistant machine's CPU can take several minutes; the answer is also on the app's page.

init.description: Tip: for voice satellites, make a dedicated Home Assistant user with no admin rights, choose it below, and mark it as a child in the Household Assistant app (Admin → People), so a voice in the room can only ask about that user's own things.

error.bad_key: The key must be at most 200 characters, without spaces.

recorder_keeps_messages.title: The recorder keeps the household apps' messages
recorder_keeps_messages.description:
The household apps' questions and answers travel as {event} events, and Home Assistant's recorder keeps them in its history. Add this to configuration.yaml, then restart Home Assistant:

```yaml
recorder:
  exclude:
    event_types:
      - {event}
```
